introduction: An earlier guide treated the Covenant as the safeguard of unity. This one gathers what ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says of it as a power: the artery in the body of the world, the spirit by which a soul is “born again,” an ark, a fortress, a tree whose shade covers humanity, a lamp like the morning star. Its tests are severe in proportion to its greatness, some who were favoured fall away, and the firm are promised protection and confirmation. The guide ends in prayers for steadfastness. Almost every image has a history in the Bible and the Qur’án, and the outside quotations trace it: the vine and the branches, Noah’s ark and the bow in the cloud, the tables written with the finger of God, Jeremiah’s new covenant, the Qur’án’s “firm hand-hold,” the foam that passes and the truth that has come, the tree of life, the new Jerusalem. A few readings are set against other voices: Jesus eating with sinners and Paul’s “admonish him as a brother” beside the command to shun; Jeremiah’s question why the faithless prosper; Elijah’s “I only am left”; and Kant on freedom.
questions: The Covenant is called “the pulsating power in the arteries of the body of the world.” What does the image of an artery say that the image of a fortress does not?

“Shun those who are shaken in the Covenant,” and “‘Abdu’l-Bahá loves all no matter how they turn away from Him.” Read Paul’s “count him not as an enemy.” How are avoidance and love held together in practice?
“The tests of every dispensation are in direct proportion to the greatness of the Cause.” Why would a clear, written Covenant make the tests more severe?
Many who had received great favours later wavered. What do the readings, Hebrews and the letter to Ephesus suggest about how firmness is lost?
“Whoever shows the slightest wavering … will immediately fall … even in this mortal world.” Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper. In what sense is the promise true?
The power of the Covenant is said to give “the true freedom of the Kingdom.” How can a bond be a source of freedom? Compare the vine and the branches.

outside.why: “The pulsating power in the arteries of the body of the world is the spirit of the Covenant.” Jesus’ image for the same dependence: I am the vine, ye are the branches; without me ye can do nothing.
Whoever is vivified by it “is born again.” The phrase is from Jesus’ night talk with Nicodemus: except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.

Bahá’ís are to establish the oneness of mankind; “if they cannot unite around one point how” will they do it? Jesus’ prayer gives the same reason for unity: that they all may be one; that the world may believe.
“This mystic oneness.” The first community in Jerusalem: the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.
“No soul becomes alive except through the spirit of the Covenant.” Jesus: this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.

Whoever enters a city should become “the center of attraction” by his sincerity, honesty and kindness. A second-century writer on how Christians were known in theirs: they dwell in their own countries, but simply as sojourners; they obey the prescribed laws, and at the same time surpass the laws by their lives.
“Who can resist the power of the Covenant?” Gamaliel’s counsel: if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
“If all the world should combine to overthrow the Covenant, it could not succeed.” Isaiah: the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but the covenant of my peace shall not be removed.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá “never changes in His love for them.” Paul: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God.
Bahá’u’lláh “brought us from the most remote countries of the East and acquainted us with you.” Jesus: many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down in the kingdom of heaven.

Hearts of East and West connected. Kipling’s famous line says never, and his next lines say when: there is neither East nor West, Border, nor Breed, nor Birth, when two strong men stand face to face. What does the meeting take, in Kipling’s ballad and in this reading?

Whispers “as cold as midwinter” are spread “hoping to wither the soil of the hearts.” Jesus on seed that springs up and is scorched: when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.
Shield souls from “veiled suggestions and secret whisperings.” Paul: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.
“For five and twenty years did He nurture everyone.” Hosea, in God’s voice: I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms; but they knew not that I healed them.
“Shun those who are shaken in the Covenant.” The Letter to Titus: a man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.

Shunning is commanded. Jesus was blamed for the company he kept: why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners? He answered: they that be whole need not a physician. Whom did Jesus sit with, and whom does this reading mean? Are they the same kind of person?

Paul also told a church to withdraw from a member, and added a limit: have no company with him; yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother. How does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s “He never changes in His love for them” compare?
Without the Covenant “you would have witnessed the dispersion of the believers.” Paul foresaw it for his own churches: after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you.
“The divine sheep must constantly be guarded against devouring wolves.” Jesus: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep; the hireling seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep.

“Whatever he says is correct.” The nearest claim in Christian history was defined in 1870 for the Bishop of Rome when he speaks ex cathedra. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s authority rests on a document in Bahá’u’lláh’s hand. What difference does the manner of appointment make to a claim of this kind?
“An impregnable fortress and a mighty stronghold.” Proverbs: the name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
The Book of the Covenant is “incontestable, being in his own handwriting.” Paul authenticated his letters the same way: ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
The first covenant document: two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.
“Make haste, make haste towards the forgiveness and mercy of thy Lord!” Isaiah: seek ye the Lord while he may be found; let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him.
The “Sure Handle” of the old Scriptures is the Covenant. The phrase is the Qur’án’s: whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold.
Some behave “as if the Blessed Beauty had not taken a Covenant.” Moses had the book of the law placed beside the ark, that it may be there for a witness against thee.

“In no previous Dispensation was there a Covenant and Testament of such magnitude and clarity.” The Letter to the Hebrews made the same comparison in its day: the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
“In the feast of the Covenant such a covenant was taken.” The Qur’án’s first covenant, taken from all souls before time: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify.
No covenant like this has appeared. Jeremiah had promised a new one, of a different kind from the old: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers; I will write it in their hearts.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s silence was to teach the friends firmness “whether ‘Abdu’l-Bahá should remain or pass away.” Paul to a church he could not visit: not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence.
“God hath made My hidden love the key to the Treasure.” The First Letter of John: we love him, because he first loved us.
“This is the Day that shall not be followed by night.” John’s vision of the holy city: and there shall be no night there.

“The worth of all acts is conditioned upon His acceptance”; without recognition and love, the cry is not heard. Paul: though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

“The divine Jerusalem has come down from heaven. The bride of Zion has appeared.” ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words are those of Revelation: I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
Bahá’u’lláh “renewed the basis of the religions of God.” Revelation: behold, I make all things new.
“Forget not God’s covenant within your souls.” Moses: beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God.
“Believe not everyone who attributeth himself to Us.” The First Letter of John: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God.
“The Covenant of God is … the ark of salvation.” Jesus on the days of the first ark: they did eat, they drank, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came.
The covenant that followed the flood: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
“Victory, in the first instance, is belief in God and recognition.” The First Letter of John: this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.
Even the angels “have entered beneath its shade.” A psalm: he that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
Leave “the vain imaginings of the doubters and hearken to the true and honest Word explicitly set forth.” Isaiah: to the law and to the testimony.
The power of the Covenant will “secure for the captive in the hand of nature the true freedom of the Kingdom.” Paul: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

Freedom through a covenant of obedience. Kant defined freedom of mind as release from tutelage: have courage to use your own understanding. What is the “captive in the hand of nature” freed from, and is that the freedom Kant meant?
Mountains stand firm by the attraction at the earth’s centre, and firmness in the Covenant needs “the attractive force of heart and soul.” Dante: the Love which moves the sun and the other stars.
“Let them grow and develop in the Garden of Thy Covenant.” The first psalm: like a tree planted by the rivers of water; his leaf also shall not wither.
“The fire that was kindled on the holy Mount Sinai of the Covenant.” Exodus: the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

“The Tree of the Covenant hath been planted in the midst of Paradise” and “cast its shadow over all humanity.” Revelation: the tree of life; and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.

The Iroquois Great Law gives a covenant of nations the same image: roots have spread out from the Tree of the Great Peace, and any nation may trace the roots to the tree and be welcome to take shelter beneath it.
The Tree grows despite sword and axe. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án; in Pickthall’s English: We reveal the Reminder, and lo! We verily are its Guardian.
“The lamp of the Covenant is like the morning star.” Revelation: I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.

The Covenant “is a star that gleams.” The Second Letter of Peter on the word that guides through the dark: a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.
The Sun is veiled, and “the splendours of the Most Great Light have grown stronger.” Jesus prepared his disciples for the same paradox: it is expedient for you that I go away.
“The true and radiant morn is the dawn of the Covenant.” Proverbs: the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
“Take hold of this cup … Drink and give to drink.” The shepherd psalm: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

Become “the Jamshíd of these days.” The poets of Persia used Jamshíd’s cup and court for the opposite lesson: the Lion and the Lizard keep the courts where Jamshyd gloried and drank deep. What kind of wine does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá offer that the ruin cannot touch?
Whoever comes under the Banner of Praise is safe. The Song of Songs: he brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
With this Lamp before his face, a person’s “forehead shall glisten with manifest light.” Moses coming down with the tables of the covenant: the skin of his face shone.
The True Tailor has clothed the world in a robe woven of the lights of the Covenant. Isaiah: he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness.

“The tests of every dispensation are in direct proportion to the greatness of the Cause.” The First Letter of Peter: the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án on a victory of the firm. The verse: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.
Until the wavering appear, the banner is not raised. Jesus’ parable lets both grow together until the harvest, and only then are they told apart.
The First Letter of John on what a departure shows: they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.
“They are in an impregnable fortress.” A psalm: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed.

“Do not consider that I am alone … I alone resist all the nations.” Elijah said nearly the same under a juniper tree: I, even I only, am left. He was told of seven thousand who had not bowed the knee. What does the loneliness of the faithful look like from inside, and what does it miss?
“They secretly make people weak in the Covenant.” Paul to converts who had been unsettled: ye did run well; who did hinder you? A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
Whoever holds fast “shall remain safe and protected from all tests.” Jesus: my sheep hear my voice; neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
Without one point “a thousand sects would have formed.” Corinth: every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos. Is Christ divided?
“Remain steadfast in this matter with the utmost power and strength.” Paul: be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.
“God hath promised to protect thee.” Isaiah: fear thou not; for I am with thee: I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
“Henceforth be not grieved. The Cause hath been and shall ever be in God’s hands.” Jesus: in the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

“Christ had eleven people at His ascension - then observe what happened.” Gibbon on what happened: a pure and humble religion finally erected the triumphant banner of the cross on the ruins of the Capitol.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án on foam. The verse: as for the foam, it passeth away as scum upon the banks, while, as for that which is of use to mankind, it remaineth in the earth.
“This edifice is made of steel.” Jesus: upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
“Look not to your own power and capability.” Zechariah: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
Many who had received favours and long Tablets “in this day wavered.” The Letter to the Hebrews on those who were once enlightened and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and fall away.
The letter to Ephesus: thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen.
“This dust and these clouds cannot conceal the Sun of the Covenant.” John: the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
The Covenant is “the pulsing artery … the connecting force among all.” Paul’s body: the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth.
As “the Old and New Testaments” carried the Cause of Christ, so the Covenant now. Testament and covenant are one word in the Gospel: this cup is the new testament in my blood.
“Neither give ear to commendation and praise, nor be saddened … by censure.” Paul: with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment.
“This is the Call of the Covenant … the gift that the Day-Star of the world hath graciously given.” Luke’s angel: I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
“The slightest discord among the friends is like deadly” poison while the Tree is under test. Jesus: every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.
Whoever holds firm, “the company of the angels … will confirm him.” A psalm: he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

Whoever wavers “will immediately fall, becoming frustrated and disappointed even in this mortal world.” Jeremiah, a faithful man, saw the faithless doing well and asked God about it: wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? How should such a promise be read when experience seems to go the other way?
Without constancy, “a harvest of knowledge and certitude is not worth a grain of mustard seed.” James: he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
The Centre of the Covenant asks that his “servitude … lowliness … brokenness” be proclaimed. Paul of Christ: he took upon him the form of a servant.
“If we have Him with us we are invulnerable.” A psalm: the Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

The Báb to his first disciples: “My Covenant with you is now accomplished … the Lord of the Covenant shall assuredly assist you.” Jesus’ parting words to his: lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
“Be not dismayed.” The charge to Joshua: be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed.
Respect is due to the well-known supporters of the Cause “so long as they remain firm.” Jesus: he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
A prayer to be among those who “observe Thy Covenant.” A psalm: what shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me? I will take the cup of salvation.
“Ye have plighted your troth … ye have drunk deep from the chalice of loyalty.” Ruth to Naomi: whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.

“Bring them together again, O Lord … gather their dispersion.” God in Ezekiel: as a shepherd seeketh out his flock, so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered.
In an ocean of trials “we have an Ark of Salvation.” The Letter to the Hebrews: which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.
“Can it be possible that … the feet of any one shall slip?” The closing blessing of Jude: unto him that is able to keep you from falling.
The same fear of slipping, turned into a request in one of the psalms: hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
That he “may confirm the weak in Thy Covenant.” Jesus to Peter: when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
“The rays shining forth from the Lamp of the Covenant.” A psalm: thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
A prayer for the steadfast, that they may be “signs of guidance.” The oldest blessing in the Bible: the Lord bless thee, and keep thee: the Lord make his face shine upon thee.

genesis-my-bow-in-the-cloud.text: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth

john-neither-shall-any-man-pluck-them.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand

galatians-ye-did-run-well.text: Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth? This persuasion cometh not of him that calleth you. A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump

hebrews-anchor-of-the-soul.text: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil

revelation-bright-and-morning-star.text: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star

quran-grasped-the-firm-hand-hold.text: Whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold. Unto Allah belongeth the sequel of all things.
